card.name: Verbs of one drug affecting another
card.fires_on: The verb (or linking word) right after a drug name or 'not' that says one drug does or does not affect another's levels, such as alter, affect, increases, or 'effect on'. It appears in drug-interaction sections.

modes.label: Negated effect verb
modes.description: Verbs like alter or affect after 'did not' or 'does not' in interaction findings.
modes.example: Nifedipine did not<< alter>> the plasma levels of vardenafil hydro

modes.label: Effect on another drug
modes.description: 'on' or 'increases' linking one drug to a change in another drug's levels.
modes.example: Voriconazole also significantly<< increases>> efavirenz plasma concentrations [see

modes.label: Non-drug 'saving' verb
modes.description: A rare plot-summary verb where one character does something to another's life.
modes.example: , Alvaro saves his life in a tavern brawl. Both use assumed names while fighting in Naples against the Germans, when Carlos returns the favor by<< saving>> Alvaro's life.

card.writes: It seems to prepare the model for an object noun like pharmacokinetics or levels of the second drug.
card.plain: It marks the verb in sentences saying one drug does or doesn't change another drug's blood levels.
